newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai minister vows to boost flagging exports.
newsitem.headline: New Thai minister vows to boost flagging exports.

text.p: Thailand's new commerce minister, Narongchai Akrasanee, on Wednesday outlined his strategies for boosting the nation's sagging exports and maintaining price stability.
He told reporters his priorities on exports would be to develop new export products to replace those that have become less competitive and to expand into new export markets.
Narongchai was speaking after a meeting with a senior Commerce Ministry official and said he would release the ministry's export targets for 1997 this weekend.
"We must keep our traditional markets while developing new ones. Latin America and Eastern Europe are among new potential markets," he said.
Exports, which have been Thailand's biggest foreign exchange earner for years, have grown only marginally this year due to structural and cyclical problems, analysts said.
The latest central bank data show that Thai exports in the first nine months of this year grew only 0.9 percent, compared to more than 20 percent in the same period last year.
Narongchai proposed setting up a trade representative office in the ministry to promote Thai exports and negotiate trade disputes abroad.
On price stabilization, Narongchai, a well-known free trade advocate, said he would support freer competition and curb monopolies to stabilise prices.
He said he would also back further removals of import quotas on certain raw materials such as grains, which are used in the feed industry.
But he declined to answer questions on whether there would be further cuts in some existing import tariffs.

"Problems that cause price instability in foods such as pork meat and poultry have nothing to do with tariffs but rather with the import quota (of raw materials). If there is anything we can do with the quota to benefit consumers, we will," he said.
Thailand recently lifted import quotas on soymeal and soybean.
